questions.stem: Two frontoparallel squares have equal physical side length H and depths Z and 2Z. Separately, two distinct parallel straight lines lie in one plane at fixed camera depth Z0>0, parallel to the image plane. In an ideal pinhole camera, which paired conclusion is correct?
assumptions: Same physical H, orientation and focal length; no distortion; Z>0.

options.text: The farther square has half the image side length; the two lines meet at a finite image vanishing point.
The farther square has one quarter of the image side length; the two lines remain parallel in the image.
The squares have equal image side lengths; the two lines remain parallel in the image.
The farther square has half the image side length; the two lines remain parallel in the image.

citations.evidenceText: Parallel edges in the world are projected as lines that converge toward a vanishing point; the farther cube face appears smaller.

solution.justification: Perspective size varies inversely with depth. The source explanation overgeneralizes parallel-line convergence: lines parallel to the image plane remain parallel, so the finite vanishing-point claim requires a direction with nonzero depth component.

optionExplanations.o2: The size conclusion is right, but lines parallel to the image plane have no finite vanishing point.
optionExplanations.o3: The parallel-line conclusion is right, but equal physical size at different depths does not imply equal image size.
optionExplanations.o4: One quarter is the projected area ratio, not the image side-length ratio.

questions.stem: A NumPy array is created as I=np.array([230], dtype=np.uint8). Compare a uint8 addition of 50 with an explicit float conversion before addition. What values result from (I+np.uint8(50))[0] and (I.astype(float)+50)[0], respectively?
assumptions: One-element uint8 array; both addends of the first operation are uint8; float conversion occurs before the second addition.

citations.locator: Assignment physical page 29: Week 7 Q3, uint8 value and addition premise
citations.evidenceText: uint8 image I contains a pixel with value 230; O=I+50.

citations.locator: Assignment physical page 30: Week 7 Q3 continuation, modular working and conversion note
citations.evidenceText: 230+50=280; 280 mod 256=24; conversion from uint8 to floating point is important.

solution.justification: The arithmetic path, not merely the displayed output type, determines whether overflow is retained.

optionExplanations.o1: The uint8 result wraps modulo 256; conversion before addition preserves the real-valued sum.

optionExplanations.o3: Casting before addition avoids the wrap; casting the already-wrapped result would give 24.0.
optionExplanations.o4: 280 cannot be represented by uint8; the first addition retains that dtype.

steps: Unsigned 8-bit integers have 256 residue values, 0 through 255.
Converting 230 to float before adding yields 280.0, without uint8 overflow.

misconceptions: 255 is saturation, not the stated modular uint8 array addition.

questions.stem: A 28×28×1 input passes through 16 square convolution filters with stride 1, zero padding and dilation 1. The output spatial size is 24×24. What are the kernel spatial size and full output shape?
assumptions: Standard valid convolution with unit dilation; channel-last shape notation.

citations.evidenceText: Input 28×28×1; stride 1; padding 0; 16 kernels; output spatial dimensions 24×24; K=5 and output 24×24×16.

solution.justification: Spatial size is determined by kernel geometry, stride and padding; channel count is determined by the number of filters.

optionExplanations.o3: The spatial kernel is right, but output channels count filters, not input channels.
optionExplanations.o4: This confuses number of filters with kernel width; K=16 would give 13×13 spatial output.

steps: Sixteen filters give sixteen output channels: 24×24×16.

assumptions: Dilation 1; square input/kernel; independent output channel per filter.
